title: Networking — OutboundNat
description:
Purpose: deterministic per-host bridge/tap/IP/MAC allocation, default-deny iptables policy with admitted DNS resolvers and bounded private exceptions, ownership-aware idempotent cleanup.
Contract: bridge/tap names + CIDR + IPv4 + MAC are deterministic functions of (run_root, vm_id) via sha256; collisions fail closed; rules tagged for ownership cleanup; bridge orphans only removed when no peer references them.

title: Address allocation
description:
Contract: bridge name brfc + first 12 hex of sha256(run_root); bridge CIDR 172.<o2>.<o3>.0/24 from sha256 bytes (o2 = (sha256[0]%16)+16, o3 = sha256[1]); cap of ~4096 non-colliding bridges per host (172.16.0.0/12); tap name tfc + first 12 hex of sha256(run_root+vm_id); guest IPv4 deterministic per (run_root,vm_id); guest MAC 02:+hex of vm_digest[0..5] locally-administered.

title: Adapter ecosystem & agent surface
description: Purpose: ship the agent-facing layer ON TOP of m80's generic core, so m80 stays auditable while the agent UX matches or beats SmolVM. Scope decision (2026-05-03): the originally-planned external 'm80-adapter' moves in-tree as 'm80-adapter'. Agent semantics (tool catalog, idempotency, semantic events) remain OUT of m80 itself per CLAUDE.md scope; they live in this adapter layer. Strategic context: SmolVM (CelestoAI, shipped Apr 2026) owns 'Python AI sandbox'. m80's edge is Rust-embeddable + audit-small + generic foundation. Adapter ecosystem extends reach without contaminating the core: m80-adapter (Rust agent surface), m80-py (PyO3 Python bindings), CLI agent mode.

title: m80-adapter crate (in-tree, on top of m80-firecracker)
description: Contract: a thin Rust crate exposing tool-catalog semantics (bash, exec, read_file, write_file) and structured responses on top of m80-firecracker's generic exec. Idempotency keys, semantic events (sandbox_exec_started/_succeeded/_failed/_timed_out), workspace policy enforcement. ~500-1500 LOC. Surface: Adapter::new(Backend), Adapter::tool_call(req), AdapterError. Evidence: docs/behaviors/adapter/*.md + crates/m80-adapter/tests/*.

title: Persistent-state VM lifecycle (relax one-exec-per-VM)
description: Contract: a RunningSandbox supports multiple sequential exec calls (today the README pins one-exec-per-VM). Required for agent UX: a multi-turn agent shouldn't pay cold-boot latency between turns. Surface change in m80-firecracker: RunningSandbox::exec(req) becomes &mut self instead of self; add Sandbox state-transition tests covering the multi-exec path. Evidence: docs/behaviors/lifecycle/persistent-state.md + crates/m80-firecracker/tests/persistent_state.rs.

title: Python bindings (m80-py via PyO3)
description: Contract: a PyO3 wrapper around m80-adapter exposing the agent surface to Python (parity with SmolVM's installable surface, but on top of a Rust core). ~300-500 LOC. pip install m80. Surface: m80.Sandbox class, m80.tool_call(...). Evidence: crates/m80-py/* + a Python-side smoke test that pip-installs and runs an exec.

title: CLI agent mode (m80 agent run --tool ... --args ...)
description: Contract: a 'm80 agent' subcommand exposing the adapter's tool-call surface from the command line for ad-hoc use. Surface change in m80-cli: add 'agent' subcommand. Evidence: crates/m80-cli/tests/agent_mode.rs.

title: Foundation positioning docs (README + adapter pattern + SmolVM comparison)
description: Contract: project README + a docs/positioning.md page that frames m80 as the auditable libfirecracker foundation, with the adapter pattern (Rust agent / Python bindings / CI runner / 'your adapter here') as the legible extension story. Honest comparison with SmolVM (CelestoAI, shipped Apr 2026) — when to use which. Lead non-AI use cases (untrusted-PR CI, multi-tenant SaaS isolation, build farms) so the foundation isn't read as agent-coupled. Evidence: README.md + docs/positioning.md.

title: Warm-pool / Blank VM Allocator (active v0.2 — agent latency parity)
description: Warm-pool / blank-VM allocator for sub-200ms exec latency. STATUS CHANGED 2026-05-03: was deferred-deadcode (vocabulary-only, allocator unwired); now active for v0.2 because warm-pool is the dominant unlock for agent-latency parity with SmolVM (advertised <200ms cold). Without warm pool every adapter exec pays a 1-2s Firecracker cold-boot, which makes m80 unusable for multi-turn agent workloads even with the m80-adapter shipped (epic m80-qokt). The reset-evidence vocabulary (Reusable | Discard) and non-inference rule under this epic are still load-bearing — they're the contract a warm-pool implementation has to honor. Pairs with epic m80-qokt.2 (persistent-state lifecycle) — together they make multi-turn agent UX viable.
